scope.intended_use: A coordinated left/right indoor bookend pair whose visible front facade is formed by large, tightly spaced name glyphs. The wood appearance uses the physically preferred direct-sampled candidate C on the glyph fronts. Revision 0.4.1 must deepen the glyph bodies and strengthen the more deeply recessed rear connection without turning it into a visible rectangular panel; the existing side-blade and inward-foot architecture carries the books.
scope.user_context: Adult indoor use on a flat shelf or desk; requested MARITA pair with contour-balanced MA | RITA split; sequential FFF printing on the recorded Anycubic Kobra 3 Max profile with 0.4 mm nozzle and 0.12 mm layers. The user printed the 0.4.0 STL and reports that the letters do not look sufficiently stable where they join; no measured load, deflection, fracture, material identity, or photo is recorded.
variants: default name STEFAN split STE | FAN
requested name MARITA; planned automatic contour-balanced split MA | RITA
0.4.1 reinforced facade requirements proposal: 12 mm glyph depth and stronger rear connector
out_of_scope: Wall mounting, stacking, child-directed use, structural shelving, or loads beyond the approved physical test
Automatic printer upload or print start
Claiming candidate C as equivalent for another material, machine, nozzle, orientation, relief depth, pattern, or physical scale without another controlled coupon

entities.name: Mirrored side-blade and inward-foot functional core
Fused large-glyph facade with recessed connector web and wood relief

evidence.uncertainty_note: The 0.3.0 foot geometry is retained, but 0.4.0 load and slide tests have not run.

failure_modes.mode: Foot slides or tips on the shelf
failure_modes.effect: The book row may lean or fall and may cause minor item or surface damage.
failure_modes.mitigation: Retain the inward weighted foot and run the defined pair load/slide test on the intended shelf condition.

acceptance_criteria: With the defined 2.0 kg row there is no tip, fracture, permanent set, or slide beyond 5 mm.

interfaces.name: Side blade and foot support the book row

evidence.uncertainty_note: The nominal retained load path is defined, but no 0.4.0 physical proof load exists.

failure_modes.mode: Side blade, foot, or gusset cracks under lateral book load
failure_modes.effect: Loss of book-retaining function with limited property damage.
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep decorative glyphs out of the primary load claim and repeat geometry, slicer, and physical pair tests on 0.4.0.

acceptance_criteria: The complete pair passes the 2.0 kg book-row test without fracture, tip, permanent set, or excessive slide.

interfaces.name: Glyph facade joins the functional core through a recessed rear web
keepouts_and_access: Do not fill glyph counters or create a rectangular front panel.
Keep wood relief out of connector bonds, minimum-wall zones, the side-blade load path, and finished inter-glyph gaps.

evidence.uncertainty_note: The printed 0.4.0 result is qualitatively reported as looking insufficiently stable, but there is no force/deflection/fracture measurement. The proposed 12 mm glyph depth, 10 mm connector-front setback, 4 mm connector thickness, 2 mm positive overlap, and 12 mm bridge bands remain requirements-stage recommendations without concept, CAD section, coupon, or physical proof.

failure_modes.mode: A glyph or bridge is disconnected or breaks during handling
failure_modes.effect: Appearance failure, sharp edge, and loss of the personalized facade.
failure_modes.mitigation: Fail closed on disconnected glyph graphs or insufficient positive overlap; deepen glyphs, enlarge and recess the rear bridge structure, inspect sections and front visibility, then print a representative connector/letter coupon before the full pair.

acceptance_criteria: Every glyph is part of one watertight body; the rear connector begins at least 10 mm behind the front, overlaps glyph bodies by at least 2 mm in depth, uses at least 12 mm-wide local bridge bands, remains visually subordinate from the approved front view, and the representative coupon survives the approved handling/deflection test without fracture.

interfaces.name: Letter-only wood appearance from the intended front view

dimensions.feature: Recommended nominal gap between neighboring glyph outlines
Candidate C glyph-front maximum relief depth

keepouts_and_access: No rectangular background may define the front silhouette.
Counters and finished glyph gaps remain visibly open.
The rear connector remains untextured and begins behind the glyph body.

sources: user selection of candidate C recorded 2026-08-31
evidence.uncertainty_note: Candidate C is physically preferred on the upright planar coupon, but the new glyph mask, connector visibility, exposed flanks, exact filament, and complete profile are not yet validated.

failure_modes.mode: Texture becomes flat, gaps close, or the rear web reads as a panel
failure_modes.effect: The product no longer reads as a letter-only wooden name stand.
failure_modes.mitigation: Preserve candidate C on the glyph fronts, mask by exact glyph outlines, inspect orthographic and three-quarter views, and print a process-matched textured letter coupon.

acceptance_criteria: From the approved front view the object reads as large separate wooden glyphs; gaps and counters are visible; no rectangular background is perceived; wood relief remains recognizable under the intended lighting.

drivers: REQ=3: Appearance, personalized glyph layout, hidden connection, preserved load path, texture fidelity, and print limits are coupled.
INT=2: Shelf, books, glyph-to-core connection, and human visual/handling interfaces all require independent acceptance.
VER=3: The revision needs deterministic geometry and exact slicing plus connector, texture, handling, and complete-pair physical tests.

blocking_unknowns: Measured 0.4.0 connector deflection/fracture evidence and process-matched proof of the proposed 0.4.1 connector
Exact filament product/color/batch/conditioning and complete profile used for the preferred C print

criticality.rationale: The retained bookend load is modest and static; credible failures are appearance loss, a broken decorative glyph, or limited item/surface damage rather than high-energy or safety-critical harm.
credible_failure_effects: loss of intended book-retaining or personalized appearance function
sharp edge if a decorative bridge breaks

decision.rationale: The retained functional core, approved 0.4.1 reinforcement requirements, and physically preferred C texture route permit a controlled sectioned concept. No 0.4.1 production CAD or export is permitted before concept approval. Release additionally requires a connector/glyph coupon, exact slicing, and full-pair physical tests.

warnings.message: The printed 0.4.0 facade is reported as looking insufficiently stable. The proposed deeper glyphs and stronger connector are not yet supported by an approved sectioned concept, generated body, measured deflection, or physical handling coupon.
The preferred C print confirms appearance qualitatively, but the exact filament identity, conditioning, and complete slicer profile remain unknown.

At the approved 122 mm cap height, the planned MA | RITA split has only about 1.25 mm X margin to the 350 mm per-part design envelope; exact generated bounds and slicer bed placement must pass before this variant is a print candidate.

next_actions.action: Generate and approve a sectioned 0.4.1 reinforcement concept before production geometry.
next_actions.exit_criterion: The concept shows 12 mm glyphs, a 4 mm rear connector starting 10 mm behind the front, at least 2 mm positive overlap, 12 mm local bridge bands, open counters, visible gaps, and no rectangular front panel.

next_actions.action: After concept approval, generate and test a reinforced letter/bridge coupon before rebuilding the complete MA | RITA pair.
next_actions.exit_criterion: The coupon preserves candidate C on the front, retains at least 1.2 mm finished gaps, keeps counters open, remains visually letter-dominant, and passes the approved handling/deflection test.
